blind_spots.blind_spot: Battery life is benchmarked to a consumer smartwatch (48 hours) with no SWaP-C framing for continuous cockpit/combat monitoring.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A fighter pilot on a multi-hour sortie or extended training cycle needs uninterrupted EOG/EKG data; a 48-hour civilian battery claim says nothing about flight-line recharge access, in-flight power draw, or spares logistics — the SWaP-C and sustainment questions the checklist flags.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The FAQ answering this question is written for athletes and coaches, not for a DAF end-user managing a fielded pilot monitoring system.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: This depends on the use, but a fully charged battery lasts 48 hours similar to your Apple Watch.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Data architecture is Bluetooth-to-cloud with no DDIL framing, despite the SBIR target use case being in-cockpit and combat monitoring.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A cockpit or contested airspace during a combat sortie denies the continuous connectivity this architecture assumes — the same frame-rate/bandwidth failure mode the checklist's crowd-detection example describes — and neither the site nor the SBIR abstract explains how data reaches storage when disconnected.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The Bluetooth/cloud description was written for the sports product line, then reused as the technical story for the DoD contract without adapting for a contested RF environment.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Nextiles data is real-time and transmitted through Bluetooth. Our data is stored both in the cloud and locally.

blind_spots.blind_spot: No ATO/RMF, CMMC/NIST 800-171, or ITAR language anywhere, despite the product collecting physiological data on DAF personnel and transmitting it wirelessly.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Biometric monitoring data on a warfighter is sensitive PII moving over RF into DoD systems — that typically triggers an ATO/RMF review before any Phase III production decision, and a compliance story limited to 'machine washable, no degradation after 20 cycles' hasn't engaged the gate that actually kills transitions.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Phase II goals as stated are entirely about wearability and prototype delivery, not data governance or network authorization.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: The main goals of our involvement in this project are: Test and manufacture EXG electrode materials for skin-voltage pickup Develop mock prototype to assess comfortability, wear, and user-experience of the device.

opener_hook: Your AFWERX Phase II abstract puts fabric EOG/EKG sensors on a fighter pilot's helmet for cognitive-load monitoring — the battery spec on your site is benchmarked to an Apple Watch's 48 hours.
what_they_do: Fabric-embedded biometric sensor wearables for athlete performance, adapted under a separate AFWERX contract to monitor fighter-pilot cognitive load.
